items.title: ‘It Feels Like I’m in a Nightmare’: Inside the First Deportation Flight to Iran
items.description: For decades, Iranians fleeing persecution have found protection in the United States. But this fall, the Trump administration deported a planeload of people to Iran after making a deal with Tehran.

items.title: Dismantled by DOGE, a Foreign Policy Center Finds New Life
items.description: The Kennan Institute, which researches Russia and the surrounding region, has re-emerged in a form that is smaller but more impervious to government control.

items.title: For Trump, Nothing Was Off Limits During the Shutdown
items.description: President Trump pressured Democrats by taking punishing actions no previous administration ever took during a shutdown.

items.title: Shutdown Deal Revives Democratic Infighting
items.description: The agreement prompted a backlash within the party, not only against the Democratic defectors who supported it, but against Senator Chuck Schumer, the leader who did not.

items.title: Trump Asks Supreme Court to Overturn Verdict in E. Jean Carroll Case
items.description: The president said the assertions behind a judgment that he sexually abused and defamed the writer were “implausible” and “unsubstantiated.”

items.title: Trump Pardons the Husband of a Republican Congressional Ally
items.description: Robert Harshbarger Jr. pleaded guilty in 2013 to health care fraud and distributing a misbranded drug. His wife, Diana Harshbarger, is a member of Congress.

items.title: Age Is the Issue That Democrats Can’t Shut Down
items.description: A restless Democratic base is seething at older leaders in Washington.

items.title: Travelers Battle More Flight Disruptions Amid Shutdown Talks
items.description: The travel turmoil led some fliers to embark on time-consuming detours as they monitored talks in Washington to end the government shutdown.

items.title: Groups Sue to Reverse Trump’s Cuts to Energy Projects in Democratic States
items.description: A lawsuit filed on Monday argued that the president has discriminated against blue states by slashing federal funds for political leverage during the shutdown.

items.title: Spending Bill Would Pave Way for Senators to Sue Over Phone Searches
items.description: Republicans have voiced outrage that Jack Smith looked at G.O.P. lawmakers’ phone records surrounding the Jan. 6 attack. Legislation to reopen the government would allow them to sue for $500,000 each.

items.title: More Flight Troubles Expected Before the Shutdown Ends
items.description: Airlines brace for further chaos, even as eight Democratic senators broke ranks with their party to back a deal that could end the shutdown.

items.title: Jeanne Shaheen Faces Shutdown Blowback From Her Daughter
items.description: Senator Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire voted to move to end the shutdown. But her daughter Stefany Shaheen, a congressional candidate in their state, sharply criticized the deal.

items.title: Supreme Court to Hear Major Challenge to Mail-In Ballot Laws
items.description: The justices agreed to hear a challenge to Mississippi’s law, a case that could upend similar measures in dozens of states before the 2026 election.

items.title: Supreme Court Denies Request to Revisit Same-Sex Marriage Decision
items.description: Kim Davis, a Kentucky county clerk who refused to issue same-sex marriage licenses, had asked the court to reconsider its landmark 2015 opinion.

items.title: Bernie Sanders Endorses Peggy Flanagan for Senate in Minnesota
items.description: Senator Bernie Sanders is backing Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan in her state’s Democratic primary race for Senate, his latest attempt to pull the party to the left.

items.title: U.S. Military Kills 6 in Strikes on Suspected Drug Boats, Hegseth Says
items.description: The latest strikes raised the death toll in the campaign to 76 people in 19 attacks in the Pacific and the Caribbean Sea since early September.

items.title: Trump Administration Returns to Supreme Court in Food Stamp Fight
items.description: But the administration indicated it might not be necessary, as Congress moved toward a deal to fund the government.

items.title: Which Senators Broke Ranks With Democrats to Advance the GOP Plan to End the Government Shutdown?
items.description: Two of them are retiring, and none of the others face re-election in 2026.

items.title: Senate Passes Bill to Reopen Government Amid Democratic Rift
items.description: The vote, on Day 41 of the shutdown, signaled an end in sight to weeks of gridlock. Eight members of the Democratic Caucus supplied the critical backing.

items.title: Syria’s President Meets Trump at White House for First Time
items.description: The visit by President Ahmed al-Shara is another step in the transformation of the former rebel leader once wanted by the United States as a terrorist.

items.title: The Supreme Court will hear a challenge to grace periods for mail ballot returns
items.description: The Supreme Court will hear a case that could decide whether states can count postmarked mail ballots that arrive after Election Day — something that about 20 states and territories currently allow.

items.title: COVID vaccine rollout and pandemic preparedness assessed in new book, 'Fair Doses'
items.description: In his new book, 'Fair Doses,' epidemiologist Seth Berkley discusses what went right -- and wrong -- with COVID vaccine distribution and whether the world is ready if a new pandemic were to strike.

items.title: 'Nuremberg' is full of big questions — and missed opportunities
items.description: The new film portrays Hitler's second-in-command, Hermann Goering, as a wily mastermind, sidestepping uncomfortable questions about how unexceptional evil can be.

items.title: Senate approves legislation to end shutdown. And, where climate change efforts stand
items.description: The House returns to vote on a bipartisan bill that could end the government shutdown. And, at the COP30, data show the world is still far from meeting its climate goals.

items.title: 9 strategies to find free or low-cost food when money is tight
items.description: Kevin Curry, a food influencer and a former SNAP recipient, explains where SNAP recipients can get the most up-to-date information on their benefits, and how anyone can find free or affordable food.

items.title: I'm pregnant but my doctor won't see me before 9 weeks. Why not? Is it OK to wait?
items.description: A pregnancy test can tell you that you're expecting as early as 4 weeks, but most doctors won't see you for another month. Many women want care sooner. Why's it so hard to get and what can you do?

items.title: How to avoid 'The Winner's Curse'
items.description: A new book by the Nobel-winning pioneer of behavioral economics offers some advice we can all use.

items.title: A suicide bomber targets an Islamabad court, killing 12 people and wounding 27
items.description: No group immediately claimed responsibility for the explosion, which also wounded at least 27 people, but Pakistan has struggled over the past months with a resurgent Pakistani Taliban.

items.title: Trump floats tariff 'dividends' even while plan shows major flaws
items.description: President Trump says the government will distribute checks to Americans from tariff revenue. Here's what that could mean.

items.title: Climate negotiations have started. Here's how far countries need to go
items.description: Nations have begun climate negotiations at the COP30 summit in Brazil. Studies show the world is not on track to avoid the most damaging impacts of climate change.

items.title: Judge’s ruling likely to give Democrats a congressional seat in Utah
items.description: The ruling is a blow for Republicans in the broader national redistricting battle between the parties ahead of next year’s midterms.

items.title: Democrats push for a ‘ruthlessly pragmatic’ approach to counter Trump
items.description: There were seething accusations of capitulation at eight Democratic-aligned senators who broke ranks to join Republicans in voting to end the shutdown.

items.title: When neighbors lost SNAP benefits, the internet stepped in to feed them
items.description: People are influencing politics and increasingly finding food for their families by telling their stories of economic struggle online in ways that were not possible even a few years ago.

items.title: How women feel about Trump’s presidency: Heartbreak, fatigue, gratitude
items.description: We asked women how they felt about Trump right after he won the election. One year later, we caught up with them to see how they feel now.

items.title: How every senator voted on the bill to reopen the government
items.description: See how your lawmaker voted.

items.title: Trump says staunch ally Greene has ‘lost her way’
items.description: The Republican congresswoman accused the White House of focusing on foreign affairs instead of domestic ones.

items.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to intervene in SNAP fight again
items.description: The battle over funding for the nation’s largest anti-hunger program has left millions wondering how they will afford food.

items.title: Supreme Court won’t hear challenge to landmark gay marriage ruling
items.description: The announcement indicates there is not an appetite among the high court’s conservative majority to revisit one of the court’s most significant decisions in recent years.

items.title: Supreme Court to decide if mail-in ballots may arrive after Election Day
items.description: An appeals court found that federal law requires all ballots to be received by Election Day.

items.title: Trump pardons Giuliani, other allies who sought to overturn 2020 election
items.description: None of the more than 75 people listed have been charged with federal crimes, though several have been prosecuted in states.

items.title: U.S. strikes two more alleged drug boats, pushing death toll past 75
items.description: The attacks in the eastern Pacific Ocean, disclosed Monday by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, killed six people, he said.

items.title: The health care battle behind the shutdown roils North Carolina politics
items.description: The health care debate has become a “microcosm of the midterms” in the battleground state as rising premiums hit.

items.title: Appeals court denies Trump effort to halt full SNAP benefits for November
items.description: Back-and-forth court rulings have led to confusion and frustration over SNAP subsidies that help 42 million recipients pay for groceries.

items.title: These are the Democrats who broke ranks to vote for the shutdown deal
items.description: Sens. Dick Durbin, Tim Kaine and others supported a deal paving the way to end the shutdown. A final deal would need support from the House and president.

items.title: A Rastafarian goes to the Supreme Court after a prison shaved his dreadlocks
items.description: The question is not whether Damon Landor was mistreated but whether he can sue the individual prison officials and guards for damages.

items.title: More than 10,000 flights delayed in worst day of disruptions since shutdown
items.description: More than 2,800 flights were canceled Sunday, while Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy said the shutdown’s impact on airports is “only going to get worse.”

items.title: Late-night Senate deal opens path to ending shutdown but splits Democrats
items.description: The deal that split Democrats doesn’t extend expiring ACA subsidies. If a bill passes the Senate, it needs the House to approve and President Donald Trump on board.

items.title: Trump administration orders states to pause paying full SNAP benefits
items.description: As the shutdown dragged on, USDA demanded that states “immediately undo” any steps they have taken to send full November payments to SNAP recipients.

items.title: Ten seconds in the Oval Office that overshadowed Trump’s drug-price win
items.description: A press conference collapse has sparked days of memes and jokes. Not all are accurate.
